verdict.rationale: Glama lets developers connect a GitHub repository and have it built from source, or ship a Dockerfile, npm package or PyPI module. Servers are private by default and can be flipped to a public registry listing, with ownership claiming via an account-bound token. Each registry page includes pre-filled install config blocks for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and VS Code, and community developers confirm publishing and updating their own MCPs with quality scoring. Missing for 10: documented publishing steps (the credit-card requirement for rebuilds/releases was undocumented and cost users days), and guidance on discoverability for new listings among the large catalog.
